title: "Native electrolyte estimation and dependent Born diameters"
execute:
  enabled: false

The retained comparisons support native least-squares fitting of molality-scale
mean ionic activity, practical osmotic coefficient, single-ion solvation energy,
solvent transfer energy and bulk relative permittivity using exact Engine first
parameter derivatives. Three dependent Born diameters hold declared hydration
energies during fitting. This is **numerical verification** of #219 slice A and the guarded minimax path,
with the conditions and identified wheel below. It establishes no #209
parameter adoption, global optimum or physical validation.

## Basis and calculations

All cases use the temperature and pressure declared in [the native inputs](scripts/declarations.py), on the liquid branch. The source parameter
packet is Figiel `/4`; the [input hashes](inputs/files.json) and
[declarations](scripts/declarations.py) identify each component subset and row.
The 383 F1 rows include chloride/bromide activity and osmotic coefficients,
transfer and hydration energies, and water/alcohol permittivity or ratios.
Undefined ethanol-methanol pair data are not supplied: each observation uses
its source-defined component subset. Absent components have no parameter column.

The native coordinate chart solves

$$
H_i=RT\ln\phi_i^\infty-G_{i,target}=0,\qquad
\frac{dd_i}{du_a}=-\frac{H_{i,\theta}D_{ind,a}}{H_{i,d}}.
$$

Its inner criteria bound energy error in J/mol and exact correction
or refined bracket width in Angstrom, as declared by [the holds](scripts/declarations.py). Both estimators use the complete map for their exact first columns. Ceres uses
it for its conditional covariance. Final checks rebuild from the stored
parameters, preserving solved diameters without another hold solve.

The exact physical columns and independent central differences test the same
reported quantities. The manufactured recovery uses seven free coordinates,
three native holds and 156 native manufactured rows. The perturbed-data case
adds +0.005 decade to NaCl activity observations and compares the three stored
diameters against independently refined native scalar roots.

The [equation owners](../../engine/docs/equations.md),
[parameter-regression formulation](../../engine/docs/regression/science/pure-saturation-regression.md)
and [algorithm owners](../../engine/docs/science/algorithms.md) define the
pressure chart, admitted finite reference, reported activities and held map.

### Fitted versus cold osmotic replay

The [current rerun](results/minimax.json) completes both declared minimax
starts under the original budgets and retains [every comparison](results/minimax.csv).
The [diagnosis and previous failures](results/minimax-diagnosis.json),
[native contraction operands](results/minimax-density-operands.csv) and
[wheel comparisons](results/minimax-wheel-comparisons.csv) identify a
one-ulp mixture-density change between the fitted evaluator's accepted density
seed and a fresh cold closure. The pure-water density and fitted physical
parameters agree. A native probe reproduces both original osmotic predictions
by changing only that admitted mixture density.

The [exact native density sensitivity](scripts/density_sensitivity.cpp) uses the
residual Helmholtz gradient and Hessian to differentiate the common-pressure
Euler expression at fixed temperature, composition and pure-water reference.
Its derivative-times-ulp estimate is much smaller than the observed binary64
change and has the opposite sign. The [leaf derivation](README.md#current-minimax-replay-757)
and [retained sensitivity values](results/minimax-diagnosis.json) distinguish
smooth density propagation from changes in rounded Helmholtz and
chemical-potential operands. The one-ulp density change triggers those rounding
changes, which are amplified in the osmotic equation by division by the small
solute-to-solvent particle ratio.

The repair replays both point evaluators at each fitted optimizer point with
common cold density initialization. Prediction comparisons keep their original
limits. Stored-fit minus cold predictions remain explicit initialization
diagnostics, and the fitted candidate's exact columns, holds, chart and stored
checks keep their existing assertions. The derivative estimate is not treated
as a bound on binary64 rounding. This rerun awaits independent review and
supports numerical verification of manufactured observations only.

## Affine parameter columns and native input construction

The original affine-column discrepancy concerned the reported derivative basis.
The public `optimizer_gradient` reports a prediction derivative; the native
`residual_optimizer_gradient` reports the pre-division residual derivative at
unit row weight. The fitter consumes the residual derivative, and minimax
consumes the prediction derivative. The [basis operands](results/affine-column-basis.csv),
[original failed comparison and refinement operands](results/affine-column-comparisons.csv)
and [conditions and wheel identity](results/affine-column-diagnosis.json)
preserve that diagnosis. Independent refinement did not explain the original
basis mismatch; the correction changed the reader meaning used by the study.
It changed no thermodynamic derivative or numerical tolerance.

The native start, signed reciprocal action and manufactured one-coordinate
recovery are retained in [the numerical comparisons](results/affine-coordinate-recovery.csv)
and [their input declarations and criteria](results/affine-coordinate-recovery.json).
The proportional packing and Debye-Huckel lengths follow the declared sigma
coordinate. An inconsistent tied length is rejected. Independently written
reciprocal pairs verify the density action, and a manufactured aqueous
activity/osmotic fit recovers the declared scalar while preserving its held
hydration energy. These comparisons test coordinate construction and the
residual chain; they establish no physical parameter adoption or identifiability.

The [qualified affine operands](results/affine-coordinate-qualification.csv)
and [conditions, derivative meanings and wheel identity](results/affine-coordinate-qualification.json)
retain the held and unheld column comparisons, refinement uncertainties,

## Meaning and limits

Reference values and columns belong to the admitted finite dilution endpoint.
Terminal changes and a finer witness admit each consumed column; they do not
certify a universal infinite-limit bias. The retained permittivity identity,
density-chain and limiting-column checks have their quantities and criteria
in [the comparison rows](results/falsifiers.csv).

The recovered point and perturbed-data roots demonstrate the complete
held-coordinate calculation at the declared branches. The perturbed fit
reaches active bounds, so covariance is withheld. Convergence does not prove
a global minimum. Interior covariance describes conditional local sensitivity
with fixed hydration targets and independent weighted errors; Gibbs-Duhem
links gamma and Phi, so it does not describe measurement uncertainty.

The [diagnosed misses](results/diagnosed-failures.json) retain the scalar
cancellation causes. Prescribed-pressure ln Z removes unequal terminated
pressure logarithms from reference energy differences. The extensive
Helmholtz Euler identity stabilizes the dilute solvent difference before
formula-unit division, with extended-precision scalar accumulation.
Parameter columns remain exact CppAD contractions. Physical definitions and
numerical tolerances were preserved.

Native multistart uses declared starts and shared budgets. Least-squares
SVD/covariance is delivered; no minimax covariance is returned. Local minimax
stationarity and guarded feasibility do not establish global optimality or
measurement uncertainty. [Code budgets](../../docs/scientific/code-budgets.md)
retain the historical allocation decisions separately from numerical evidence.

## Density initialization in fitting

At a fixed parameter point, a density-seeded evaluation reproduces the cold
evaluation within the owner's equivalence standard: closures, association
sites, slopes, exact columns and every returned observable pass on the merged
wheel. At identical optimizer work, a seeded evaluation is about a quarter
cheaper for F2 and a few percent cheaper for B4, and the key cold equilibrium
solves do the same work as on main. No stopping control makes the complete
fits' endpoints agree within the standard's relative criterion on each
coordinate: the seeded objective differs from the cold one at the osmotic
floor, and the fits amplify that difference into their optimizer coordinates.
Under the owner's endpoint judgment, the F2 endpoints agree within
coordinate allowances carried from the accepted observable allowances through
the fit, and the B4 seeded and cold fits reach the same minimax objective.

The one round-2 osmotic comparison that exceeded a plain relative criterion
concerned conditioning, not a changed state. The practical osmotic
coefficient is $\phi = -\ln a_w / s$ with $s = M_w \sum_i \nu_i m_i$
(`practical_osmotic_coefficient`). At low molality $\ln a_w$ is a small
difference of order-one Helmholtz and chemical-potential terms, so the
standard's absolute floor $\delta$ for near-zero quantities applies to
$\ln a_w$. Carried to $\phi$, each row's allowance is

$$\max\left(\epsilon_r \lvert\phi\rvert,\; \delta / s\right),$$

with $\epsilon_r$ the standard's relative criterion. The floor grows as
$1/m$. The comparison owner takes $M_w$ from the parameter packet and $\nu_i$
and $m$ from each declared observation; every other quantity keeps its
original criterion. The osmotic table reports $s\,\lvert\Delta\phi\rvert$, the
equivalent $\ln a_w$ difference, which stays at rounding level.

### Fit stops and the per-evaluation saving

{{< include results/density-initialization/round4/qualification.md >}}

[Per-iteration stopping data](results/density-initialization/round4/stop-iterations.csv),
[cold and seeded evaluations compared in order](results/density-initialization/round4/divergence.csv),
[row identities](results/density-initialization/round4/rows.csv),
[noise mapping](results/density-initialization/round4/noise.json),
[stopping-control probes](results/density-initialization/round4/stop-probes.csv),
[work-matched pairs](results/density-initialization/round4/work-matched/pairs.csv)
with [endpoints](results/density-initialization/round4/work-matched/endpoints.csv),
[pairs at the round-2 controls](results/density-initialization/round4/script-controls/pairs.csv),
[pairs at the Engine defaults](results/density-initialization/round4/engine-defaults/pairs.csv),
[key-solve work](results/density-initialization/round4/key-solves/summary.json)
and [conditions, wheel identities and source hashes](results/density-initialization/round4/provenance.json)
retain this evidence. The traces come from a local logging build that writes
each evaluation and optimizer iteration and can withhold previous-trial
offers at run time; it reproduced the round-3 endpoints and work counts
exactly. The cold comparator for the timing omits previous-trial density
offers in `fit.cpp` and changes nothing else.

The round-2 and round-3 F2 calls did not use the Engine's default stops; the
analysis declared tighter Ceres tolerances. Under them, both arms stop on the
relative-step test after their trust regions collapse. The paths first
separate at the first seeded trial, at the same optimizer point, through
low-molality osmotic rows; mean ionic activity rows agree to rounding there.
That difference is the accepted $1/s$ amplification of a rounding-level
$\ln a_w$ difference, well inside the osmotic allowance. The cost then falls
to the level where this difference decides whether a step is accepted, so the
two arms accept different steps and stop at different points inside a noise
region set by the fit's Jacobian. The seeded objective also depends on which
trial seeded it, while the cold objective repeats exactly. Tighter tolerances
leave the endpoints unchanged because both arms already stop at that floor.
Looser stops change only how far into the floor each arm goes, and the
direction of the evaluation-count difference reverses between the round-2
controls and the Engine defaults. B4's Ipopt stop is the same tolerance test
in both arms, with identical work. Its two starts reach different coordinates
at one objective, so the optimum is inferred, not mapped, to be a set; the
remaining endpoint difference is judged on the objective.

A parameter tolerance that stops F2 before the floor gives both arms
identical work and convergence, so its complete-call saving is the pure
per-evaluation saving. The per-evaluation savings at the round-2 controls and
at the Engine defaults agree with it. The round-2 F2 saving of about two
fifths therefore combined this per-evaluation saving with fewer evaluations
inside the floor. The complete call includes input and model construction,
native manufacture, holds, fitting and result reading; shared-host scheduling
adds uncertainty to the paired spread.

The timing result is the work-matched one: a pure per-evaluation saving of
24.6% for F2 and 7.0% for B4. The round-2 F2 saving of about 40% included a
path-dependent reduction in evaluations at the noise floor and is not a
per-evaluation saving.

Endpoint agreement within the standard's relative criterion cannot be reached
by stopping controls: the endpoint difference is set by the accepted osmotic
floor carried through the fit, not by the stop.

### Endpoint judgment

The owner judged the endpoints on 2026-10-06: F2 coordinates against
allowances propagated from the observable allowances, B4 by its minimax
objective. A least-squares endpoint minimizes
$\tfrac12\lVert W^{1/2} r(\theta)\rVert^2$. To first order, residual changes
$\delta r$ move it by

$$\delta\theta = -J_w^{+} W^{1/2} \delta r, \qquad J_w = W^{1/2} J = U \Sigma V^{\mathsf T}, \qquad J_w^{+} = V \Sigma^{-1} U^{\mathsf T}.$$

An observable allowance $a_i$ becomes a residual allowance
$\lvert \mathrm{d}r_i/\mathrm{d}y_i\rvert\, a_i$, with
$\mathrm{d}r/\mathrm{d}y = 1/\text{scale}$ for difference residuals and $1/y$
for log ratios. The componentwise bound on each optimizer coordinate is

$$\lvert\delta\theta_k\rvert \le \sum_i \bigl\lvert [J_w^{+}]_{k,i}\bigr\rvert \sqrt{w_i}\, \Bigl\lvert \frac{\mathrm{d}r_i}{\mathrm{d}y_i}\Bigr\rvert\, a_i,$$

with $a_i = \max(\delta, \epsilon_r \lvert y_i\rvert)$ for ordinary
observables and the osmotic allowance above for osmotic rows. The fit returns
$U$, $\Sigma$ and $V$ of the weighted optimizer Jacobian over its
positive-weight rows; the bound only multiplies these returned factors and
needs no linear solve. It is evaluated at the cold endpoint, and each arm's
rerun reproduces the retained endpoints exactly. The minimax comparison uses
the returned minimax level $t$ with allowance
$\max(\delta, \epsilon_r \lvert t\rvert)$; Ipopt's reported objective is a
fixed multiple of $t$. B4 coordinate differences are recorded as a
diagnostic of the flat optimum set and carry no criterion.

{{< include results/density-initialization/round5/qualification.md >}}

Every F2 coordinate passes at both control sets with less than a tenth of a
percent of its allowance, and both B4 starts reach the same minimax objective
within the absolute floor. The allowance is a worst case: every row moves by
its full allowance with signs aligned to one coordinate. The observed seeded
residual differences are about 1% of their allowance and concentrate in a few
low-molality osmotic rows, so the observed endpoint gaps are much smaller.
Removing the absolute floors leaves most of the allowance, so its width
reflects the relative criterion carried through this Jacobian over all rows,
not the osmotic floor alone. The bound is first order at the endpoint and
tests seeded-against-cold agreement at the resolution of the observable
standard; recovery of the manufactured truth remains the round-3 comparison.
Merging main's equilibrium polish change does not reach these fits, which
evaluate single-phase property observations only; the merged seeded wheel
reproduces the retained seeded endpoints exactly, so the timing is not
repeated.

The branch witness identifies the physical extreme within the admitted
single-loop domain; agreement with a bounded cold search remains a numerical
comparison. A cold scan with a failed grid node now refuses a sole root, while
a witnessed anchor can still close, so such a seeded state has no cold
comparator. The pressure equations, root criteria, reference ladder and exact
columns are unchanged. The delivered review of the round-2 change requested
four corrections: a density status name restored in failure causes,
seed-event assertions that make the gate falsifiers able to fail, the
endpoint comparison, and one shared Properties owner for the anchored closure
with its single cold retry. All four are in, and the endpoint judgment above
closes the endpoint comparison.

The tables present discrete comparisons in different units and paired timing
samples; a figure would add no information. This is numerical verification
and performance measurement. It establishes no physical parameter adoption,
global minimum or new physical validation, and has not received investigator
promotion for manuscript use.
